previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting, in the setting of chronic pancreatitis and Sjogren’s syndrome. Her symptoms began two days prior and worsened after a recent prednisone taper from 10 mg to 5 mg. Imaging showed no gallstones or biliary abnormalities, supporting a diagnosis of pancreatitis flare rather than a new obstructive process. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control using Dilaudid, and antiemetics. A urine culture showed contamination without evidence of infection. She gradually improved, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged on hospital day three with plans for rheumatology and GI follow-up. Key issues included pain management, steroid taper effects, and coordination of care for her chronic conditions.

# Burning Abdominal Pain with associated Coffee Ground Emesis, 
Dark Stools: The pt was hemodynamically stable for the duration 
of her hospital course. The pt presented with an initialyl 
stable Hct, that decreased with maintenance IVF (details above). 
The pt reported her symptoms were unlike prior pancreatitis 
episodes. Given the patients steroid use, the initialy 
differential included GIB, esophagitis, gastritis. Per report, 
NG lavage was refused by the patient. The pt was placed on an H2 
IV (in setting of IV PPI allergy) and had PPI increased to 40mg 
BID from 20mg. The pt stated this alleviated some of her 
abdominal ""burning"" symptoms. The pt underwent an EGD which 
revealed no signs of active gastritis. The pts nausea was 
controlled with IV Zofran. Abdominal pain was initially 
controlled with IV Dilaudid. This was weaned down and the pt was 
discharged without further scripts for PO narcotics. (The pt 
states she had PO dilaudid at home). The pt was instructed to 
follow-up with her gastroenterologist (Dr. ___ following 
discharge.

of plaquinel and prednisone 10 mg alternating with 15 mg.
